readings: Consider only accounts that have at least one row in Financial_Transactions. Join each to its customer and drop accounts whose customer is missing or whose town_city is null. For each remaining account, return: account_id; town_city; its number of transaction rows; that count divided by the total transaction rows of the remaining accounts in the same town_city; and that count divided by the average transaction count per account. Compute the average over only the remaining accounts, meaning those with a customer and a town. Return the top 10 accounts by ratio to the average, descending, unrounded.

Consider only accounts that have at least one row in Financial_Transactions. Compute the average transaction count per account over all of these accounts, before dropping any for a missing customer or town. Then join each account to its customer and drop accounts whose customer is missing or whose town_city is null. For each remaining account, return: account_id; town_city; its number of transaction rows; that count divided by the total transaction rows of the remaining accounts in the same town_city; and that count divided by the average computed before dropping. Return the top 10 accounts by ratio to the average, descending, unrounded.
queries:
WITH tx AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Financial_Transactions
  GROUP BY account_id
),
valid AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, tx.cnt
  FROM tx
  JOIN Accounts a ON a.account_id = tx.account_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  account_id,
  town_city,
  cnt AS transaction_count,
  cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER (PARTITION BY town_city) AS ratio_to_town_total,
  cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt) OVER () AS ratio_to_average
FROM valid
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
WITH tc AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Financial_Transactions
  GROUP BY account_id
),
avg_all AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM tc
),
j AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, tc.cnt
  FROM tc
  JOIN Accounts a ON a.account_id = tc.account_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT j.account_id,
       j.town_city,
       j.cnt AS transaction_count,
       j.cnt * 1.0 / SUM(j.cnt) OVER (PARTITION BY j.town_city) AS ratio_to_town_total,
       j.cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT avg_cnt FROM avg_all) AS ratio_to_average
FROM j
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
